feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Bullseye Financial Ltd enters administration
entry.summary: Bullseye Financial Ltd enters administration FCA · Oct 27, 2026 The FCA reports that Bullseye Financial Ltd entered administration on 23 October 2026, with Robert Young and Matthew Haw appointed as joint administrators. The FCA-authorised firm served only professional investors. On 11 March 2026 it agreed to a voluntary requirement to stop carrying out any regulated activity. The notice lists customer contact details and warns against scams by people impersonating the firm, the administrators or the FCA.

entry.title: FCA speech outlines reforms to UK capital markets to support economic growth
entry.summary: Reforming UK capital markets to ensure they work well for our economy FCA · Oct 5, 2026 Jon Relleen, the FCA's director of infrastructure and exchanges, gave a speech at the 2026 Reform of the UK Public and Private Capital Markets Summit. It describes the FCA's multi-year programme to reform UK capital market rules while preserving trust and market integrity. The speech covers the principles guiding the reforms, completed measures, and preparations for tokenisation and other market changes.

entry.title: FCA and Practitioner Panel 2026 survey: firms' satisfaction, confidence and trust in the FCA rise
entry.summary: Firms’ confidence, satisfaction and trust in the FCA rise FCA · Oct 2, 2026 The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and its Practitioner Panel published their 2026 annual survey of regulated firms. It finds 79% of firms are highly satisfied with their relationship with the FCA, up from 74%, and 75% report high levels of trust. Firms were most confident in the FCA's work to protect consumers, ensure markets work well and enhance the integrity of the UK financial system.

entry.title: UK FCA appoints three new Board members
entry.summary: FCA announces new Board appointments FCA · Sep 30, 2026 The UK Financial Conduct Authority has announced three new Board members. Lea Paterson CBE and Matthew Tobin were appointed by the Treasury as non-executive directors, and deputy chief executive Sarah Pritchard joined as an executive member. They take up their roles on 1 October 2026.

entry.title: FCA opens crypto firm authorisation applications under new UK regime
entry.summary: FCA opens the gateway to regulated crypto FCA · Sep 30, 2026 · Crypto The FCA announced that crypto firms can now apply for authorisation under the UK's new regime. Firms operating in the UK will be brought into full regulation, assessed against standards on consumer protection, safeguarding of customer assets, market integrity and financial resilience. Applications should be submitted by 28 February 2027, ahead of the regime's entry into force on 25 October 2027. Authorisation is not automatic, and firms that cannot meet the standards will not be permitted to operate in the UK market.

entry.title: UK FCA notice on InterestMe Financial Planning Limited (IMFP) and appointed representative InterestMe Advisers Limited (IMA) entering administration
entry.summary: InterestMe Financial Planning Limited (IMFP) and the appointed representative InterestMe Advisers Limited (IMA) enter administration FCA · Sep 28, 2026 On 24 September 2026, IMFP and IMA entered administration, with Robert Goodhew and Geoff Bouchier of Kroll Advisory Limited appointed as joint administrators. The notice explains how customers can contact the administrators, what to consider about their investments and complaints, and how to guard against fraudsters impersonating the firms, administrators or the FCA.

entry.title: FCA obtains bankruptcy order against Arthur Temlett
entry.summary: FCA secures bankruptcy order against Arthur Temlett FCA · Sep 28, 2026 The FCA asked the court to declare Arthur Temlett, trading as Abacus Insurance Consultants, bankrupt. The Sheriff granted the application on 27 August 2026, and Emma Porter of Aver Chartered Accountants was appointed trustee to assess his finances and distribute any recovered funds to creditors. The FCA had earlier, on 21 January 2025, stopped him from carrying out any regulated activities.

entry.title: UK regulator secures repayment for victims of crypto fraud
entry.summary: FCA secures money back for victims of crypto fraud FCA · Sep 28, 2026 · Crypto The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) obtained confiscation orders against Raymondip Bedi and Patrick Mavanga, who ran a fake cryptoasset investment scheme that defrauded at least 65 investors of £1,541,799. The court ordered Bedi to pay £603,404.28 and Mavanga to pay £247,997.99. Recovered funds will be returned to victims.

entry.title: FCA review of how it interacts with whistleblowers
entry.summary: Looking at how we interact with whistleblowers FCA · Oct 6, 2026 The UK Financial Conduct Authority says it has asked independent non-executive director Lea Paterson to review how it dealt with a whistleblower who had been in contact with it for many years and has died. Last year the FCA gave feedback on all 1,252 whistleblowing reports it closed, with 42% leading to direct action to manage or reduce harm. The FCA plans to share lessons from the review early next year.

entry.title: FCA proposes clearer redemption rules for long-term investment funds
entry.summary: New rules to make long-term investment funds clearer FCA · Oct 8, 2026 The UK Financial Conduct Authority has proposed rules requiring asset managers to make clear the redemption terms of funds investing in illiquid assets such as property. Investors would have to give 90 days' notice to access their money, and existing funds would have two years to comply with at least one year's notice to investors. Feedback is requested by 11 December 2026.

entry.title: UK FCA: Strong compliance functions support trust in corporate finance markets
entry.summary: Strong compliance functions support trusted corporate finance markets FCA · Oct 8, 2026 The FCA surveyed 411 corporate finance firms on their compliance resources and activities, receiving 382 responses. Most firms reported carrying out key compliance activities, but gaps remain in whistleblowing arrangements, breach registers, complaints monitoring and reporting to management. The findings ask firms to review compliance's influence, early involvement in decisions, and oversight of third-party support.</summary>

entry.title: Liam Coleman named permanent chair of Financial Ombudsman Service
entry.summary: Liam Coleman appointed as chair of the Financial Ombudsman Service FCA · Oct 9, 2026 The FCA Board, with Treasury approval, has appointed Liam Coleman as permanent chair of the Financial Ombudsman Service for a three-year term starting 10 October 2026. He had served as interim chair for the previous year. The service resolves complaints between financial businesses and their customers.

entry.title: Legal challenge to the FCA's motor finance compensation scheme to be heard in February 2027
entry.summary: Motor finance legal challenge to be heard in February 2027 FCA · Oct 13, 2026 The Upper Tribunal will hear legal challenges to the FCA's motor finance compensation scheme from 16 to 26 February 2027. The scheme is currently partially suspended, but firms must keep preparing and progress complaints as far as possible. Until the legal process concludes, lenders do not need to calculate or pay compensation under the scheme.

entry.title: Jarvis Investment Management Limited enters special administration
entry.summary: Jarvis Investment Management Limited enters special administration FCA · Oct 15, 2026 Jarvis Investment Management Limited entered special administration on 14 October 2026, with Adam Stephens and Philip Hemming of S&W Partners LLP appointed as special administrators. The FCA-authorised firm provides wealth management services. The administrators will assess client money and custody assets and decide how to return them to clients, writing to clients within 8 weeks of appointment.

entry.title: ePayments Systems Limited enters special administration
entry.summary: ePayments Systems Limited enters special administration FCA · Oct 15, 2026 ePayments Systems Limited (EPS), an FCA-authorised e-money issuer, entered special administration on 15 October 2026, with Mark Boast and Allister Manson of Opus Restructuring LLP appointed as joint special administrators. The regime adds objectives to ordinary administration, including returning customer funds as soon as reasonably practicable and engaging with payment systems operators and authorities such as the FCA. The special administrators will collect information from creditors and customers and will explain how to make a claim later.

entry.title: Revocation of LIBOR/EURIBOR-related bans
entry.summary: LIBOR/EURIBOR-related bans FCA · Oct 16, 2026 The FCA reviewed its regulatory action against individuals whose convictions were overturned by the Court of Appeal. Because those convictions were the basis for its action, it revoked the bans on Colin Bermingham, Philippe Moryoussef, Jonathan Mathew and Christian Bittar and removed the related Final Notices from FCA channels. The FCA will take no further action against these individuals on this matter.

entry.title: Building the future of finance in the age of AI: a speech by the FCA's chief data, information and intelligence officer at Bloomberg's UK Policy Series.
entry.summary: Building the future of finance in the age of AI FCA · Oct 19, 2026 Jessica Rusu, FCA chief data, information and intelligence officer, sets out the FCA's approach to safe and responsible AI adoption in financial services. She calls on firms to put consumers first, keep clear accountability and plan for failure, and publishes examples of good and poor AI practice. The speech also describes the FCA's own use of AI in supervision and plans to develop a framework for agentic finance with industry.

entry.title: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m investor losses in high-risk bonds
entry.summary: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m losses in high-risk investments FCA · Oct 21, 2026 The FCA has banned former Vector Wealth chief executive Jeffrey Dawkins from performing regulated functions and fined him nearly £270,000. He knowingly acted as a regulatory front while a disqualified director ran the firm, using its authorised status to make high-risk mini-bonds appear safer, and investors are expected to lose about £4 million.

entry.title: FCA moves Leeds office to new long-term base
entry.summary: Leeds office move FCA · Oct 22, 2026 The Financial Conduct Authority has signed an agreement for a new office at 2 Wellington Place, Leeds, which will be its long-term home there from 2028. The new site offers 36,097 sq ft of space. The current Leeds office at 6 Queen Street has grown since opening in 2022.

entry.title: FCA restricts six unregulated lenders over anti-money laundering control concerns
entry.summary: FCA restricts 6 firms following concerns over anti-money laundering controls FCA · Oct 23, 2026 The FCA imposed voluntary restrictions on six Annex 1 firms, unregulated lenders, after raising concerns about their anti-money laundering policies, controls and procedures during application assessments. The restrictions limit new customers and new business, including extending existing credit. The FCA says Annex 1 firms must show they understand their financial crime risks and have effective systems to manage them, or face action.

entry.title: Beyond borders: how regulators can address shared risks that cross firms and jurisdictions
entry.summary: Beyond borders: Regulating the risks we share FCA · Oct 23, 2026 FCA Chair Ashley Alder gave a speech on international financial regulatory cooperation at the Michael D. Gill Lecture. He argues that risks now spread horizontally across firms, sectors, supply chains and borders, so regulation must look at shared dependencies that can transmit shocks. He calls for simplifying regulation while sharpening oversight of critical services and risks outside the traditional perimeter. He also urges regulators to share intelligence, test cross-border scenarios and prepare to act together.

entry.title: FCA urges private market firms to manage conflicts of interest as the sector grows
entry.summary: FCA calls on private market firms to manage conflicts of interest in line with rapid growth FCA · Oct 23, 2026 An FCA review found that private market firms vary in how well they identify and manage conflicts of interest. It recorded good practice across private equity, private credit and real estate, but found some firms failing to keep controls current as their businesses grew more complex. The FCA expects firms to identify, record, manage and disclose conflicts effectively and show investors are treated fairly.

entry.title: Chandler King (City) Limited enters creditors' voluntary liquidation
entry.summary: Chandler King (City) Limited enters creditors’ voluntary liquidation FCA · Oct 26, 2026 Chandler King (City) Limited, an FCA-authorised independent financial adviser on investments and pensions, entered creditors' voluntary liquidation on 17 September 2026. Grace Jones and Karyn Jones of Parker Andrews were appointed joint liquidators. The firm has applied to cancel its FCA permissions, which is under FCA review.

entry.title: UK regulator's review of banking access for defence SMEs
entry.summary: Defence SMEs need banking services that work FCA · Oct 26, 2026 The FCA published findings on whether defence small and medium-sized enterprises can access banking services efficiently. It found the main issue is friction and delay, such as long onboarding and repeated information requests, rather than widespread exclusion. The FCA stresses that firms should take risk-based, proportionate decisions and that good management information supports better outcomes.

entry.title: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech at UK Digital Assets Week
entry.summary: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech for UK Digital Assets Week HMRC / gov.uk · Oct 6, 2026 · Crypto The UK Economic Secretary to the Treasury gave a speech at UK Digital Assets Week arguing for faster digitalisation of financial markets. She reports that HSBC and ClearToken have received approval to operate in the Digital Securities Sandbox and that a digital gilt, DIGIT, is planned for pilot issuance in 2027. The speech also outlines the UK's cryptoasset and stablecoin regulatory framework.

entry.title: Self Assessment deadline in 100 days: HMRC urges early tax return filing
entry.summary: Self Assessment deadline incoming – 100 days to go HMRC / gov.uk · Oct 23, 2026 HM Revenue and Customs urges Self Assessment customers to file their 2025 to 2026 tax return early, with a deadline of 31 January 2027, via GOV.UK. The announcement lists benefits of filing early and notes that UK cryptoasset owners must pay Capital Gains Tax on gains above the £3,000 tax-free allowance and declare them in their Self Assessment return.</summary>
